Most facilities reported no operational impact and safe drinking water, but the OT-focused breach at more than 30 Minnesota sites underscores exposure across enterprise SCADA and ICS deployments in critical infrastructure.

title: As Larry Ellison bets the farm, Oracle says it loves AI-written code, just not in OpenJDK
blurb: Oracle barred AI-generated code from OpenJDK contributions, even as CEO Larry Ellison pours capital into AI infrastructure, citing provenance and copyright risk in the Java platform's core codebase. The split policy shows that enterprises leaning on AI coding tools still face carve-outs where IP-liability exposure outweighs productivity gains, a signal for teams governing contributions to critical open-source stacks in their vendor supply chain.

title: One-in-five breaches are now AI-related, IBM warns
blurb: IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach report found 22% of UK firms suffered an AI-related security breach in the past year, with AI-driven attacks up 56% and the average incident now costing $6M. Deepfake impersonation led the attack types at 45%, and compromised APIs, plug-ins, and cloud misconfigurations were the most exploited entry points, pushing 61% of UK firms to raise security spending after a breach.

title: Three things you need to know about the new EU AI Act rules
blurb: Transparency provisions of the EU AI Act took effect this week, requiring organizations operating in the EU to label AI-generated content with machine-readable marks and disclose when users are interacting with chatbots, avatars, or AI agents. The rules cover deepfakes, emotion-recognition and biometric-categorization tools, and unreviewed AI text on matters of public interest, adding compliance obligations that enterprise IT teams must now build into deployed AI systems.

title: SAP dodges German antitrust investigation over data extraction
blurb: Germany's Federal Cartel Office concluded a preliminary investigation into SAP, finding sufficient data extraction options and no evidence that SAP unfairly blocks customers from moving ERP data into competitors' tools like Celonis. The regulator declined to open abuse proceedings but will keep monitoring, and a parallel US court case remains unresolved, leaving SAP's April API policy changes under continued scrutiny.

title: AI’s measurement crisis is over. The translation crisis is next
blurb: The author argues the 2025 "AI ROI crisis" was a measurement failure, not an AI failure: MIT's GenAI Divide report counted a pilot as a loss unless it showed KPI impact within six months, so projects that were never instrumented registered as failures despite $30-40B in enterprise spend. The fix is problem selection, not better models, which explains 2026's pivot to employee-facing agents in support, sales, and IT help desks where trusted metrics already exist.

title: Enterprises seek help to deploy AI as complexity mounts
blurb: Microsoft, AWS, and Google are building out forward deployed engineering teams that embed vendor talent inside customer operations to accelerate enterprise AI rollouts, with Microsoft committing $2.5B to add 6,000 engineers and AWS spending $1B on its own FDE hub. Gartner expects more than 85% of tech providers to run FDE programs as their core AI-delivery method by the end of 2026, shifting deployment cost and skills burden from strained IT teams onto vendors.

title: Workers RPC now works across Python and JavaScript
blurb: Cloudflare extended Workers RPC to work across Python and JavaScript, letting a Python Worker call methods on a TypeScript Worker (and vice versa) with no schemas, protobuf, or serialization glue. The system translates types across languages automatically, so teams can wire multi-language services together with a single Service binding and treat cross-language calls like ordinary promise- or future-returning function calls.

title: Your agent needs a computer, not a container — introducing @cloudflare/computer
blurb: Cloudflare released an early preview of @cloudflare/computer, an agent runtime that gives each agent its own computer while the platform decides whether the code runs in an isolate, a container sandbox, or a browser. The pitch is scale: Cloudflare argues there isn't enough compute anywhere to give hundreds of millions of concurrent agents their own container, so it leans on isolates that spin up fast, hibernate when idle, and store the agent's state.

title: Cloudflare Workers and Containers now support inbound TCP connections and gRPC
blurb: Cloudflare added inbound TCP and gRPC support to Workers and Containers, introducing a `connect(socket)` handler that accepts sockets from Spectrum and can route them to other Workers, Durable Objects, or containerized gRPC servers. Workers can now serve unary and server-streaming gRPC APIs via gRPC-web with automatic conversion, and Containers get full-duplex bi-directional gRPC, all available in private beta.

title: KindaRails2Shell threatens Ruby on Rails apps (CVE-2026-66066)
blurb: Researchers disclosed KindaRails2Shell (CVE-2026-66066), a critical Active Storage flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker upload a booby-trapped image and read arbitrary files off a Rails server, exposing secret_key_base and often a path to remote code execution. It hits default vips-processor setups since Rails 7, so patch to Active Storage 7.2.3.2, 8.0.5.1, or 8.1.3.1 wherever a feature serves back processed image variants.

title: Introducing the Billable Usage API: programmatic cost visibility for Cloudflare
blurb: Cloudflare launched a Billable Usage API for self-serve accounts, exposing per-product usage and cost through a single endpoint covering Workers, R2, D1, Workers AI, Vectorize, Images, and Stream. Column names map to the FOCUS FinOps spec, so teams already ingesting cost data from other providers can pull Cloudflare spend into the same toolchain, though data currently refreshes only once daily.

title: Cortex completes OSTIF security audit
blurb: Cortex, the multi-tenant long-term storage backend for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry, completed a Quarkslab security audit funded by OSTIF and the CNCF that focused on the tenant boundary and cluster operations. The whitebox review surfaced seven findings (six medium, one low), all now fixed in the latest release, alongside custom threat documentation and recommendations for future security work.

title: Smaller, faster, safer: running Kimi and GLM at scale
blurb: Cloudflare's Workers AI team detailed three techniques for serving Moonshot's Kimi K-series and Z.ai's GLM models efficiently on shared H200 GPUs: quantizing the KV cache to FP8, compressing model weights, and protecting the shared cache. FP8 KV caching doubles resident context on Kimi K2.6 from roughly 686,000 to 1.37 million tokens with no accuracy loss, packing more concurrent requests per GPU to cut per-customer cost. All benchmarks run on the open-source SGLang serving framework.

title: Geography is the latency floor you can't move
blurb: The author measured round-trip times from Tokyo to AWS regions worldwide and found a hard latency floor set by physics: 5ms locally, 166ms to US East, 373ms to Cape Town, a 70x spread that no model optimization can touch. Because the US round trip alone consumed 55–92% of the translation deadline, the biggest win came from placement, not code. Moving the inference server from the US to Tokyo cut ~160ms, more than every quantization and GPU tweak combined.

title: Hashimoto’s Superlogical bets that agentic software development needs more than a better terminal
blurb: Mitchell Hashimoto's new startup Superlogical launched a server-side multiplexer that stores authoritative session state on the server and streams raw terminal output to desktop, mobile, and web clients, letting developers and AI coding agents resume and share long-running sessions without losing context. Unlike tmux, which was built for one human watching one terminal, it tracks whether a background agent is blocked, waiting on approval, or still working, though analysts say the broader vision is unproven.

title: Secure every commit to production with Claude and GitLab
blurb: GitLab's engineering blog walks through the five handoffs in a Claude-to-GitLab security workflow, arguing that in-session vulnerability fixes cover only the moment of authoring while merges, dependency updates, and infra changes still need governance on the path to production. The piece connects Claude Security to GitLab via the MCP server, so scanning, policy enforcement, and audit-evidence collection for SOC 2, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP happen automatically. It also covers gating what code and business context leave your environment before any model sees it.

title: I Was Wrong About Marketing ROI. Here’s What $100,000,000+ in Sponsorship Sales Taught Me.
blurb: After analyzing years of data across $120M+ in SaaStr sponsorships, the author reverses an earlier position: marketing compounds for companies that already have momentum, not for those trying to spend their way out of a slowdown. The higher-ROI move is capturing existing demand, meeting prospects already in the funnel and accelerating deals in motion, rather than manufacturing demand for a product the market has cooled on. The tactical read is to concentrate spend where product-market fit is strong and treat marketing cuts during a slump as a signal to fix the product, not just the campaign.

title: Optimizing your B2B brand for autonomous AI shoppers
blurb: As B2B buyers increasingly delegate product research to AI agents, the signals that earn a citation diverge from classic SEO. Agents pull from structured data, third-party review sites, and pages with clear proprietary evidence rather than keyword-optimized top-of-funnel content. Marketers who want to be surfaced should publish specific, verifiable claims, keep product and pricing details machine-readable, and seed the review platforms and communities that AI shoppers treat as trusted sources.

title: Relevance Engineering: The New Discipline for the AI Agent Era
blurb: AI bot traffic rose 187% during 2025 while human web traffic grew just 3.1%, and agentic traffic (autonomous systems retrieving and acting on a user's behalf) jumped 7,851%, per Cloudflare. As agents research, compare, and check out inside their own interfaces, discovery and purchase collapse into one invisible interaction that breaks click-based attribution. Brainlabs argues the counter is "relevance engineering": structuring content as machine-readable context so an AI selects your brand for the specific user it serves, rather than publishing more top-of-funnel volume.

title: The bitcoin futures yield collapse: Once over 20%, now less than Treasury notes
blurb: Bitcoin futures' annualized three-month basis has paid less than the two-year US Treasury note for 157 straight days since February, the longest such stretch since the 2022 cycle low, per Glassnode. Collapsing carry has pulled monthly futures volume down to roughly $880M from February's $1.47T peak, a drop that reflects both thinning arbitrage spreads and the broader crypto bear market.

title: Robinhood wins UK crypto registration before new regulatory regime kicks off
blurb: Robinhood's UK arm was added to the FCA's register of cryptoasset companies as of July 31, clearing the regulator's anti-money-laundering requirements to offer crypto services to British users. The registration positions Robinhood ahead of the UK's comprehensive crypto framework taking effect in October 2027, whose authorization window runs from late September to February and favors firms already vetted under the existing regime alongside Ripple, Kraken, and BlackRock.

title: BlackRock expands tokenized cash with new blockchain-based money market offerings
blurb: BlackRock introduced two tokenized money market products, a share class of its Select Treasury Based Liquidity Fund (BSTBL) on Ethereum and a multichain Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle (BRSRV), both designed to qualify as reserve assets for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act. The firm already manages $60B in reserves for Circle and wants to become the industry's stablecoin reserve manager of choice.

title: Tom Lee says ether outperformed Nasdaq 100 in July as Bitmine adds 10,399 ETH
blurb: Bitmine Immersion Technologies added 10,399 ETH over the past week to reach a 5,797,813 ETH treasury worth roughly $10.9 billion, or 4.8% of Ethereum's 120.7 million-token supply, making it the largest corporate ether holder. Chairman Tom Lee said ether outperformed the Nasdaq 100 by 2,500 basis points in July, its widest monthly margin over the index in a year, while the firm bought back 16.1 million shares since July 1.

title: Bernstein says Clarity Act failure could accelerate SEC, CFTC crypto rulemaking
blurb: Bernstein said the Clarity Act's odds of passing in 2026 are fading, with the Senate holding one week before recess to move what analysts called the most consequential crypto market structure bill in US history. If it fails, Bernstein expects the SEC and CFTC to accelerate rulemaking under Project Crypto, including token taxonomy, DeFi and self-custody rules, and a finite innovation exemption from securities treatment.

title: Ripple invests in ZILO and Licuido to deepen tokenized capital markets push
blurb: Ripple made strategic investments in ZILO, a transfer agency and fund administration provider, and Licuido, an FCA-regulated tokenization platform, to bring regulated issuance, transfer agency, and collateral mobility to the XRP Ledger. The deals extend Ripple's institutional push alongside existing partners Aviva Investors, Franklin Templeton, and DBS, with RLUSD serving as the cash leg for delivery-versus-payment settlement.

title: Michael Saylor’s Strategy sells another 1,638 BTC for $105 million, reducing total holdings to 842,138 BTC
blurb: Strategy sold 1,638 BTC for roughly $104.7 million between July 27 and Aug. 2 at an average price of $63,957, cutting its total holdings to 842,138 BTC worth about $52.6 billion. The proceeds funded distributions on the firm's preferred stock and repurchases of its STRC shares, marking a continued shift from pure accumulation toward managing its Digital Credit Capital Framework.

title: Bernstein sees another leg lower for crypto markets if Clarity Act stalls
blurb: Bernstein said failure to pass the Clarity Act this year would likely trigger another leg lower in crypto markets, with the Senate running short on time before recess despite resolving stablecoin yield rules. The broker expects the SEC and CFTC to accelerate rulemaking under Project Crypto regardless, moving faster on token classifications, DeFi guidance, and self-custody rules to provide certainty without legislation.

title: BitGo launches Link, connecting clients to Coinbase, Kraken, Crypto.com and more
blurb: BitGo launched Link, a tool that connects institutional clients' accounts at Coinbase, Kraken, and Crypto.com to BitGo's platform, giving treasury teams one interface to view and move assets held both in BitGo custody and at centralized exchanges. All transfers route through BitGo's Policy Engine for governance and permissions, then auto-reconcile against exchange records through settlement, building on the firm's existing Go Network.

title: Trump Family-Linked Bitcoin Miner Posts Second-Quarter Loss
blurb: American Bitcoin Corp., the Trump family-backed miner that launched last year ahead of crypto's slide from record highs, reported a third straight quarterly loss as the value of its bitcoin holdings declined. The result underscores how mining balance sheets tied to held BTC amplify drawdowns, tracking token prices lower even when hashrate and operations hold steady.

title: South Korea’s Bithumb officially targets 2028 IPO, outlines multi-year roadmap
blurb: Bithumb, South Korea's second-largest crypto exchange, confirmed a 2028 target for its initial public offering, with plans to request a preliminary listing review in 2027 and transition its accounting from K-GAAP to the K-IFRS standard this year. The exchange is rebuilding its risk-management and internal-control framework after a 2025 delay and an incident in which an employee mistakenly distributed roughly 620,000 BTC.

title: Strategy Sells More Bitcoin, Stock as It Pushes on With Overhaul
blurb: Strategy Inc. is continuing its pivot away from steady Bitcoin accumulation, selling both BTC and its own shares to rebuild its cash reserve and shore up its capital structure. The move marks a reversal for Michael Saylor's firm, which spent years leveraging equity and debt raises to buy the token rather than sell it.

title: Bitget set to exit Japan, close all remaining positions by year-end
blurb: Bitget will halt crypto trading services for Japan residents, stopping new registrations on Sunday and force-closing all remaining positions by Dec. 31 to comply with local rules. The exit follows Japan's mid-July reclassification of crypto as financial instruments, which imposes registration requirements on foreign platforms with penalties of up to 10 years in prison and $62,800 fines for noncompliance.

title: Circle slides after Morgan Stanley downgrade, cut in price target
blurb: Morgan Stanley downgraded Circle Internet (CRCL) to underweight from equal-weight and cut its price target to $38 from $106, citing weaker reserve income and a shift toward lower-margin transaction revenue as USDC growth slows. The bank reduced its USDC supply forecasts by 33% for 2027 and 44% for 2028, and flagged rising competition from tokenized money market funds, tokenized deposits, and the new Open USD model; the stock fell 6% and is down about 30% year-to-date.

title: Bithumb now targets 2028 IPO after major internal restructuring
blurb: Bithumb, South Korea's largest crypto exchange, said it is targeting a 2028 IPO following an internal restructuring, aiming to complete risk-management assessments and align with domestic and international accounting standards by the end of 2026 before seeking a preliminary listing review in 2027. The timeline follows regulatory scrutiny over a $40B mistaken bitcoin transfer that its CEO attributed to a deficiency in internal control, and the exchange has not yet named a listing venue.

title: Strategy sold another $105 million of bitcoin last week, repurchased $81.2 million of STRC
blurb: Strategy sold 1,638 BTC for $104.73 million last week and raised another $290.6 million issuing common stock, cutting its holdings to 842,138 BTC while lifting its USD reserve to $4 billion. The company used proceeds to fund preferred dividends and repurchase 912,143 STRC shares for $81.2 million, keeping the preferred's annual dividend rate at 12% until it trades near its $100 stated value.

title: Eric Trump’s American Bitcoin treasury tops 8,000 BTC as Q2 mining production hits record
blurb: American Bitcoin, the mining and treasury firm co-founded by Eric Trump and majority-owned by Hut 8, grew its holdings 14% to 8,002 BTC in Q2 after mining a record 932 BTC. Mining revenue reached $67M at a roughly $36,500 cost per coin, though the company posted a $57.2M net loss driven mainly by unrealized markdowns on its bitcoin stack.

title: Coldcard wallet losses may near $114 million as possible fourth sweep emerges
blurb: An attacker has swept roughly 1,816 bitcoin, near $114 million, from more than 5,200 Coldcard-generated addresses since July 30, with researchers flagging a possible fourth wave tied to a 2021 firmware bug that made single-key seeds reproducible. The latest transactions use replace-by-fee, so victims who spot their coins in the mempool can outbid the attacker and move funds first.

title: Tom Lee's Bitmine bought more ether, added to stock buyback last week
blurb: Bitmine Immersion, the largest Ethereum treasury company, bought 10,399 ETH last week for about $19.1 million, lifting its holdings to nearly 5.8 million ETH, or roughly 4.8% of circulating supply. The company also repurchased 4.5 million of its own shares, part of 16 million bought back recently, as Chairman Tom Lee cited ether's 2,500-basis-point outperformance of the Nasdaq 100 in July.

title: Bitcoin, ether decline as Coldcard exploit enters a fifth day
blurb: Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $62,595 and ether dropped nearly 2% to $1,842 as a $114M Coldcard hardware wallet hack entered its fifth day, pushing some self-custody holders back onto exchanges. Derivatives signals stayed mixed, with BTC futures open interest at a one-month high, over 52% of taker volume skewed short, and options calls clustering around $68,000 and $70,000.

title: Bernstein sees another leg lower for crypto markets if Clarity Act stalls
blurb: Bernstein said failure to pass the Clarity Act this year would likely trigger another near-term selloff across bitcoin and crypto markets, citing a Senate calendar that has run short before recess despite resolved stablecoin-yield rules. The broker expects the SEC and CFTC to accelerate rulemaking under Project Crypto regardless, moving faster on token classification, DeFi guidance, and self-custody to keep tokenization and institutional adoption onshore.

title: Visa plans to acquire Israeli company BioCatch, which uses AI to detect fraud and distinguish legitimate users from attackers in real time, for $2.4B in cash (Katherine Hamilton/Wall Street Journal)
blurb: Visa agreed to acquire Israeli fraud-detection firm BioCatch for $2.4B in cash, adding behavioral-biometrics AI that distinguishes legitimate users from attackers in real time. The deal deepens Visa's push into risk and identity infrastructure beyond card rails, giving it a native tool to score transaction trust as account-takeover and authorized-push-payment fraud pressure both banks and fintech issuers.

title: BlackRock expands tokenized cash with new blockchain-based money market offerings
blurb: BlackRock expanded its tokenized cash platform with two new products, BSTBL (a tokenized Ethereum share class of an existing money market fund) and BRSRV (a multichain stablecoin reserve vehicle with daily dividend reinvestment), both designed to qualify as reserve assets for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act. The push extends BlackRock's stablecoin-reserve ambitions beyond the $60B it already manages for Circle, as it moves to become the industry's reserve manager of choice.

title: Leopold’s Fall
blurb: Net Interest dissects the collapse of Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund, which fell 67% in a month after peaking at $45B in assets, up fivefold in three months. The author frames the blowup through Steve Cohen's three risks (liquidity, leverage, and concentration) and notes the death spiral resembled a bank run, with positions publicly tied to the fund attacked as margin calls forced liquidation. The public book was down roughly 85% stripping out private holdings like Anthropic.

title: Robinhood wins UK crypto registration before new regulatory regime kicks off
blurb: Robinhood's UK arm was added to the FCA's register of cryptoasset firms as of July 31, clearing the regulator's AML requirements and joining over 50 approved companies including Kraken, Ripple, BlackRock, and BNY. The registration positions Robinhood ahead of the UK's comprehensive crypto framework taking force in October 2027, where the authorization window runs from late September to February and already-registered firms have done much of the compliance groundwork.

title: Visa to buy cybersecurity firm BioCatch for $2.4 billion amid surge in AI-powered scams
blurb: Visa agreed to acquire fraud-detection firm BioCatch for $2.4B in cash, adding behavioral biometrics that flag scammers and bots by keystroke timing and touchscreen pressure. The deal expands Visa's fast-growing value-added services business and pushes fraud screening upstream of settlement, as generative AI makes account takeovers cheaper to run and scams cost the global economy over $1T a year.

title: Ripple invests in ZILO and Licuido to deepen tokenized capital markets push
blurb: Ripple made strategic investments in ZILO, a transfer agency and fund administration provider, and Licuido, an FCA-regulated tokenization platform, to add regulated issuance, transfer agency, and collateral mobility to its XRP Ledger infrastructure. The deals extend Ripple's institutional stack, where RLUSD serves as the regulated cash leg for delivery-versus-payment settlement, and build on existing tokenization work with Aviva Investors, Franklin Templeton, and DBS.

title: James Dacombe’s Olix raises at $3.3bn valuation
blurb: Olix, the UK AI-chip startup founded by 25-year-old James Dacombe, raised $312m led by Fundomo at a $3.3bn post-money valuation, roughly tripling its $1bn mark from February and drawing backing from Arm, Hudson River Trading, and Reed Hastings. The company aims to undercut Nvidia on price and speed with chips that skip supply-constrained components, and has hired former Wise CFO Matt Briers ahead of a chip tape-out later this year.

title: Nigeria’s Top Bank Offers $1 Billion Shares Held by Bridge Firm
blurb: First HoldCo Plc, parent of Nigeria's largest lender First Bank, plans to raise about 1.4 trillion naira ($1 billion) through a share sale after the Central Bank of Nigeria approved the offer of stock previously held by a bridge firm. The raise strengthens First Bank's capital base against the CBN's higher minimum-capital requirements for banks, which have pushed the country's largest lenders toward equity offerings ahead of the 2026 recapitalization deadline.

title: Circle slides after Morgan Stanley downgrade, cut in price target
blurb: Morgan Stanley downgraded Circle Internet (CRCL) to underweight and cut its price target to $38 from $106, citing weaker reserve income and a shift toward lower-margin transaction revenue as USDC growth slows. The bank trimmed USDC supply forecasts by roughly 33% for 2027 and 44% for 2028, pointing to competition from tokenized money market funds, tokenized deposits, and the new Open USD model as pressure on Circle's earnings.

title: Why the UK’s new BNPL rules are an opportunity to rethink credit
blurb: The UK's new Deferred Payment Credit framework brings BNPL under FCA oversight, and the author argues its real significance is prompting retailers to reconsider who owns the customer relationship rather than treating compliance as the endpoint. As regulation narrows the gap between DPC, instalment lending, and interest-free credit, product labels matter less than the embedded experience, giving retailers a reason to reclaim credit journeys from third-party providers.
